Apply [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk) or [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision) for the selected record.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e8a14639d6c2512ed5f9bfea0f7bfd9d4a2e428642e8fc8a02d600f792ab846f\"}, {\"heading\": \"links-for-decisions-and-risks\", \"title\": \"Links for decisions and risks\", \"anchor\": \"links-for-decisions-and-risks\", \"start_line\": 132, \"end_line\": 149, \"content\": \"## Links for decisions and risks\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 any artifact type | `concerns` | Names every artifact the question is about. |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ), Specification (SPEC), Verification contract (VER), Architecture (ARCH), Architecture decision (ADR), or Work order (WO) | `blocks` | Names artifacts whose transitions the decision (DEC) blocks. Each must also appear in `concerns`. |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ), Specification (SPEC), Verification contract (VER), Architecture (ARCH), Architecture decision (ADR), or Work order (WO) | `produces` | A decision (DEC) in `decided` names artifacts its answer created or amended, when applicable. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 any artifact type | `threatens` | Names the artifacts the risk (RISK) could damage. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 Work order (WO) | `mitigated_by` | Names the work orders (WO) reducing a risk (RISK) in `mitigating` or `mitigated`. The decision operation writes this link. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 Architecture decision (ADR) or Decision (DEC) | `avoided_by` | Names the single architecture decision (ADR) or decision (DEC) that removes a risk (RISK) in `avoided`. The decision operation writes this link. |\\n\\nA decision (DEC) records a question that needs an answer or a proposed deviation.\\nAn architecture decision (ADR) records a settled design choice. They serve different purposes.\\n\\nA risk (RISK) does not block work by itself. When a blocking decision (DEC)\\nis requested, that decision (DEC) concerns the risk (RISK). The `blocks` set\\nof the decision (DEC) matches the `threatens` set of the risk (RISK).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"5009680651d50038248f4c60c5fceaf6065393bf7b3b2f370c54560ba83dd63a\"}, {\"heading\": \"blocking-decisions\", \"title\": \"Blocking decisions\", \"anchor\": \"blocking-decisions\", \"start_line\": 150, \"end_line\": 175, \"content\": \"## Blocking decisions\\n\\nA decision (DEC) in `open` blocks every transition\\nof the artifacts in its `blocks` relation. A decision (DEC) in `deferred`\\nblocks transitions outside its recorded permitted scope.\\n\\nFor example, a decision (DEC) names work order (WO) `WO-EXAMPLE-001` in both\\n`concerns` and `blocks`. It is deferred with the scope\\n`WO-EXAMPLE-001:approved-in_progress`. This deferral\\nallows the work order (WO) to move from `approved` to `in_progress` if all\\nother checks pass. It still blocks moving that work order (WO) from\\n`in_progress` to `implemented`. The deferral also records when the decision\\n(DEC) must be revisited. Deferral does not itself start the work.\\n\\nAn accepted deviation is a decision (DEC) with `kind = \\\"deviation\\\"`,\\n`status = \\\"decided\\\"`, and `disposition.option = \\\"accept\\\"`.\\nIt records permission to depart from one identified specification (SPEC)\\nrule; \\u201caccepted\\u201d is not a separate lifecycle state for the decision (DEC).\\n\\nThat deviation remains applicable to the affected specification (SPEC),\\nwork orders (WO), and their verification records (VREC) and release records\\n(RLS) until a later decision (DEC) against the same rule reaches\\n`status = \\\"decided\\\"` with `disposition.option` set to `amend` or\\n`supersede`. The disposition is written through `harnessctl decide`, not\\nby editing the metadata by hand.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ed29cb785085f0704b9ab61f95ab42f2ee01579c0d191cb6587ce6c97684cdc0\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h44\\\\f\\\\codex-421\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"risk\", \"title\": \"risk\", \"anchor\": \"risk\", \"start_line\": 188, \"end_line\": 198, \"content\": \"## risk\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Record a description, an owner and a next action.\\n- Use `harnessctl raise-risk --description TEXT --action TEXT --owner ROLE` with a domain and title.\\n- Stage, category, threatened artifacts and scoring are optional. If scoring is useful, supply likelihood and impact together (1\\u20135); the command computes their product.\\n- Request `--with-decision` only when the owner needs a decision that blocks named artifacts. A risk by itself does not block work.\\n- Keep earlier scores, decisions and dispositions as recorded; no migration is required.\\n\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8815c9ff38ca34594404ab95cb0545053e209804030f3d635a50641d33559de9\"}, {\"heading\": \"decision\", \"title\": \"decision\", \"anchor\": \"decision\", \"start_line\": 171, \"end_line\": 187, \"content\": \"## decision\\n\\nA pending question becomes a `decision` (`DEC-`) when it blocks a transition\\nof another artifact, concerns more than one artifact, or must survive the\\napproval of the artifact that raised it. Below that threshold the actor asks\\nand the answer stays in the transition's `reason`.\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `kind` is `question` (an ambiguity met while authoring or planning) or `deviation` (an implementation cannot meet one rule of one specification). *(mechanical)*\\n- One `question`, `raised_by`, at least two `[[options]]` with `id` and `label`, and a `recommendation` naming one option. *(mechanical)*\\n- A deviation also names `against = \\\"SPEC-xxx#PREFIX-AREA-NNN\\\"`, a rule identifier the specification defines *(mechanical: E-DCM-005)*, and the `observed` fact; its options are drawn from `amend`, `supersede`, `accept`, `stop` and include `stop`. *(mechanical)*\\n- `concerns` names every artifact the question is about; `blocks` names the artifacts that cannot change state while it is `open`, each also in `concerns`. *(mechanical)*\\n- The `[disposition]` table is written by `harnessctl decide`; a hand-written one is `E-DCM-003`. A deferral needs a scope and a revisit trigger; accepting a deviation needs a revisit trigger. *(mechanical)*\\n- `decided` and `withdrawn` decisions are never deleted or rewritten.\\n- The definition templates carry no `Open decisions` section: a definition's pending decisions are the `DEC-` artifacts that name it in `blocks`, and the approval gate reads them from the graph. A legacy section, where one remains, reads `None` or lists `DEC-` identifiers; prose there is `E-DCM-004`.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"b3fdcc8578aac9039cf6513b13851f7a35a63027fde6dd1afeb34593a23e083b\"}]}]}\r\n",
  "exit_code": 0,
  "status": "completed"
}

Before review, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and [AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation](AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation). Before approving work, read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification). For an open or deferred decision, read [RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"9aa32693606102a5aa74b2e4a614aed6904471e5f618dea93356baac97c86ca2\"}, {\"heading\": \"resolve-approval-blockers\", \"title\": \"Resolve approval blockers\", \"anchor\": \"resolve-approval-blockers\", \"start_line\": 84, \"end_line\": 159, \"content\": \"### Resolve approval blockers\\n\\n**Inputs:** The findings from [Assess the proposed artifact package](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#assess-the-proposed-artifact-package) and the affected draft artifacts or\\npending decisions (DEC).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Corrected drafts within the proposed scope. Where an\\n  actual human decision is supplied, the selected decision (DEC) receives its\\n  disposition. A paired risk (RISK) may change through that same operation.\\n- **Transient working material:** The resolution of each finding and any\\n  remaining dependency requiring an amendment or another human decision.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Correct incomplete or inconsistent draft content within the requested scope.\\n2. Return an accepted-definition change to the amendment procedure in\\n   \\u201cDefine the change.\\u201d Do not edit accepted authority to clear a check.\\n3. For a blocking decision (DEC), inspect its current question and options.\\n4. Obtain the accountable human's exact answer if it has not already been given.\\n5. Preview that disposition with the command below.\\n6. Apply the same command with `--apply` only if its inputs match the actual\\n   decision and the preview passes.\\n7. Read back the decision (DEC) and any paired risk (RISK).\\n8. Rerun the checks affected by the corrections. Preserve unresolved blockers.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact DEC-ID --json\\nharnessctl decide REPO --artifact DEC-ID --option OPTION-ID --decision ACTOR --reason \\\"Exact decision reason\\\" --json\\n```\\n\\nUse a declared option ID. Add `--revisit \\\"Trigger\\\"` for acceptance of a\\ndeviation. A risk-mitigation option also requires `--mitigated-by WO-ID` for\\neach selected mitigating work order (WO). For a risk-avoidance option, use\\n`--avoided-by ARTIFACT-ID` when naming a separate architecture decision (ADR)\\nor decision (DEC). Review the returned operation before applying it.\\n\\nACTOR is the actual human who made the decision. If that human acts under an\\nexisting owner label, first resolve their authority under\\n[Decision rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights), then add\\n`--authority-owner OWNER` to both preview and apply. For example, a human\\nnamed `mmzen` acting under `engineering-owner` uses\\n`--decision mmzen --authority-owner engineering-owner`. Do not put the owner\\nlabel in place of the human. Neither string authenticates the decision.\\nOWNER must be non-blank printable text of at most 128 characters and match\\nan eligible owner exactly. An unrelated label refuses without writing.\\n\\nFor an explicitly authorized deferral, use this preview instead:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl decide REPO --artifact DEC-ID --defer --scope ARTIFACT-ID:FROM-TO --revisit \\\"Trigger\\\" --decision ACTOR --reason \\\"Exact decision reason\\\" --json\\n```\\n\\nRepeat `--scope` for each permitted transition. For an explicitly authorized\\nwithdrawal, replace the option or deferral arguments with `--withdraw`.\\nApply a passing preview by repeating the exact command with `--apply`.\\nThen inspect the decision (DEC) again and rerun validation:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact DEC-ID --json\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\n```\\n\\nIf proposing a departure from a `SHOULD` rule, record the rule ID, reason,\\nimpact, accountable human or agent, and compensating evidence. Present these\\nwith the affected review finding. Recording the departure does not authorize\\nan action or waive a required check.\\n\\n**Completion:** Each blocker is resolved or assigned an explicit outstanding\\ndecision. A deferral clears only its recorded transition scope.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Obtain the human's decision](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#obtain-the-humans-decision) receives the corrected package. Unresolved blockers\\nremain visible and prevent the affected approval.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ead7ade46e1090c644d789a5ca1155415aa2497561938b885e8316cd13aeb920\"}]}]}\r\n",

The score describes the knowledge expected from the reader, not the quality or complexity of the document. -->\\n\\n> This is a non-authoritative reference to command syntax, actors and side\\n> effects. The selected released evaluator computes lifecycle states, allowed\\n> transitions, gates and next actions. Start with\\n> [ENGINEERING_HARNESS.md](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md#read-selected-instructions) (resource `ENGINEERING_HARNESS.md`, heading `read-by-task`), then use\\n> [CONTINUE.md](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md#read-selected-instructions) (resource `docs/engineering/harness/CONTINUE.md`, heading `continue-selected-work`),\\n> [decision rights](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md#read-selected-instructions) (resource `docs/engineering/harness/AUTHORITY.md`, heading `decision-rights`) and\\n> [results](harness-installation-and-upgrades.md#read-selected-instructions) (resource `docs/engineering/harness/RESULTS.md`, heading `report-a-lifecycle-result`) when directed.\\n\\n## Invocation\\n\\nIn evaluator examples, `harnessctl` means the absolute Python executable of\\nthe repository's selected released evaluator followed by `-I -m se_harness`.\\nRun it from outside the checkout. `REPO` is the absolute repository path;\\nreplace placeholders before running a command. Source-development commands\\nare identified separately and do not govern repository lifecycle state.\\n\\nFor example, with `CHECKER` replaced by that absolute executable:\\n\\n```text\\n\\\"CHECKER\\\" -I -m se_harness check \\\"REPO\\\" --artifact WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nIn PowerShell, prefix a quoted executable with `&`. Run\\n`harnessctl COMMAND --help` for the exact parser help in the selected environment.\\nThe syntax inventory below shows parser defaults and optional inputs; always\\nsupply an absolute `TARGET` for repository operations from the external directory.\\n\\n## Command shape\\n\\nThese rules describe the local evaluator commands (`WO-ECP-022`).\\nThe unpublished hosted `remote` client has the separate contract below:\\n\\n- **The repository is the positional `TARGET`**, default `.`, on every\\n  command that reads or writes one. `select-work-order` reads an event file,\\n  `identity` reads a runtime environment and `qualify candidate-package`\\n  reads a wheel, so they take none. `skill-ownership` requires an explicit\\n  positional `TARGET` under SPEC-PLG-020; it has no implicit repository selection.\\n- **Naming.** `--artifact` selects an existing artifact; `--id` names the\\n  record a command creates; an option that names a relation of that record\\n  keeps the relation's name (`--work-order`, `--verification`,\\n  `--verification-record`, `--release-contract`). Both record commands name\\n  their preparation actor `--owner`. `preflight` keeps `--work-order`\\n  until it folds into `check`.\\n- **`--json` everywhere.** The workflow commands print the schema-2 result;\\n  `validate`, `validate-draft`, `inspect`, `resources`, `release-unit`, `identity`\\n  and `qualify` print their own objects; every other command prints one\\n  `se-harness-command-result-v1` object with the same facts as its human\\n  output.\\n- **Plan and write.** A command that changes existing governed state\\n  (`transition`, `decide`, `upgrade`, `skill-ownership`) plans by\\n  default and writes only with `--apply`. A command that adds content\\n  (`init`, `scaffold-domain`, `create-artifact`) writes by default and\\n  plans with `--dry-run`; `init` into a target with content appends the\\n  bounded fragments to existing files and refuses every other difference.\\n- **Exit codes.** `0`: completed. `1`: the command ran and its result is\\n  failed, blocked or not passing. `2`: the command could not run (a usage\\n  error, a refusal before any result). A failed result goes to standard\\n  output in both renderings; a code appears once per line.\\n\\n## Command inventory\\n\\n| Command | Principal actor | State effect | Intended use |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| `remote` | authorized sandbox operator or author; reader for reads | explicit remote reads or bounded sandbox draft writes; no local fallback | use the separate\", \"offset\": 0, \"next_offset\": 4096, \"complete\": false, \"characters\": 64034}\r\n",
