  "aggregated_output": "{\"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h44\\\\f\\\\codex-421\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\reference\\\\server\\\\contracts\\\\lifecycle-v2.md\", \"sha256\": \"9f1c02ef540c00fa739beb6521295ba9b068f3ab66ff0b0b196cb95810dcd601\", \"bytes\": 5989, \"text\": \"# Private lifecycle rehearsal wire contract\\n\\nThe v2 endpoint accepts only `lifecycle-v2.json`. Every request and result selects\\ntest data. Git remains authoritative for real work. Existing v1 routes and the\\nseven read-only MCP tools keep their contract; they cannot dispatch v2 actions.\\nIn an explicitly configured test project their results use\\n`se-harness-graph-read/v2`, with a required test-copy label. Ordinary Phase 2\\nprojects retain their v1 read result shapes. Revision byte hashing is unchanged;\\ntest revisions add explicit test-copy provenance, without rewriting v1 fixtures.\\n\\n`inspect` accepts check, preflight and validate. `preview` runs a mutation in a\\ndiscarded projection and returns its input digest and complete proposed file\\neffects. `apply` requires that digest, reruns the released checks, and commits\\nthe complete result once. A preview never changes graph state. Actor strings\\nare synthetic test inputs, not authenticated human consent.\\n\\nThe digest binds project/context versions, all selected revision IDs, retained\\nsnapshot, exact command/file inputs, principal and released evaluator identity.\\nMode and operation key are excluded from the preview binding, but included in\\nthe accepted request digest used for principal-scoped retry lookup.\\n\\n## Permitted file effects\\n\\n| Action | Permitted effects in the disposable projection |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| check / preflight / validate | No file writes |\\n| transition | Only selected newly authored artifacts and evaluator sidecars declared by their records |\\n| decide | Selected new decision and its explicitly linked rehearsal risk |\\n| raise-risk | New risk and optional paired decision at released domain paths |\\n| handoff | Declared bounded file inputs within the selected work order's scope; released handoff packet and evaluator evidence |\\n| capture-verification | New VREC and its released evaluator sidecar |\\n| prepare-release | New RLS and its released evaluator sidecar |\\n\\nHandoff first uses the released procedure's fixed `evidence` preparation command,\\nthen `check --checkpoint handoff --from-git`. It exposes no arbitrary evidence\\ncommand. File inputs cannot alter formal records, harness selection/instructions,\\nGit configuration, hooks, or executables used by the service. The service never\\nruns source tests. The local qualification runner supplies observed test evidence.\\n\\nThe adapter enumerates every regular file before and after the operation. It\\nrejects deletions, links, unexpected paths, missing sidecars, imported-record\\nchanges and evaluator failure before opening an acceptance transaction.\\n\\n## Snapshots and Git\\n\\nEach accepted operation retains an immutable complete snapshot: exact file bytes,\\nself-contained Git history and its source/test-candidate identities. Content\\ndigests bind the snapshot to the resulting baseline. Context heads, artifact\\nrevisions, snapshot and receipt share one database transaction. Temporary Git\\nrepositories are discarded after the result is accepted or refused.\\n\\nCapture first commits the exact input projection as test candidate P. P excludes\\nthe new VREC. The output retains the input hosted baseline B, source fixture S,\\nP and evaluator identity. Actual implementation candidate C is recorded separately\\nby qualification. Subsequent commits never alter the candidate stored in a VREC.\\n\\nExport selects an immutable baseline, checks its complete snapshot and Git bundle,\\nand returns exact bounded bytes. The installed client writes only to a new explicit\\ndestination and leaves an incomplete marker until every file hash is checked.\\nNo export writes to or synchronizes an authoritative repository.\\n\\n## Bounds and failure categories\\n\\nKeep 4 MiB requests, 2 MiB responses, 1 MiB individual file inputs, two concurrent\\nprojections, 120-second evaluator calls and 10,000 retained artifact revisions.\\nA pilot snapshot/export that exceeds the response bound is refused atomically.\\nRetained complete snapshots have a separate explicit project count bound of 128.\\nThis is a small private pilot, not an unbounded document store.\\n\\nBoundary/malformed requests, stale inputs, evaluator refusals, invalid output and\\nunknown transport outcomes remain distinct. Read the operation receipt after a\\nlost reply. A changed request under the same accepted key is a conflict. The\\nservice does not automatically rerun a mutation at a newer version.\\n\\n## Bounded Cypher reads\\n\\nThe existing `cypher` MCP/HTTP read selects one exact view. Its request uses the\\nread schema, not the lifecycle command schema. Read the public labels and\\nproperties in [the physical representation](../../docs/notes/hosted-artifact-graph.md#physical-representation)\\nbefore selecting a query. `Artifact` and `Revision` are distinct public labels.\\n\\nThe admitted form has one `MATCH` or `OPTIONAL MATCH` path, labelled nodes,\\noptional parameterized property comparisons, `RETURN`, and a numeric `LIMIT`.\\n\\nRelationship paths are supported. Use `-[edge:TYPE]->` or `<-[edge:TYPE]-` between\\nlabelled nodes, with a public relationship type from the physical representation.\\nEach node and relationship needs a distinct variable name. Anonymous relationship\\nsyntax such as `-[:TYPE]->` is refused; a refusal of that form does not mean\\nrelationship traversal is unsupported. Return-column aliases (`AS alias`) are\\noptional.\\n\\nFor example, with `parameters` containing a selected artifact ID under `artifact`:\\n\\n```cypher\\nMATCH (r:Revision) WHERE r.artifact_id = $artifact RETURN r.artifact_id AS id, r.status AS status LIMIT 10\\n```\\n\\nUse the response's completeness fields with the requested row/byte/depth budget.\\nThis example supplies no project filter: the service binds the selected project\\nand view. Unlabelled nodes, `WITH`, aggregation and arbitrary database syntax are\\nnot part of this small public read form. A rejected query has not completed a read.\\nKeep the exact refusal; consult the documented form before constructing another\\nrequest. Do not weaken query admission or bypass it through a direct database call.\\n\"}\r\n",

Before links, read [DEFINITION_LINKS.md#links-between-definitions](DEFINITION_LINKS.md#links-between-definitions). Before authoring, read [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity) and the exact type checklist linked in this file.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"fef13ff697eca3188c35b224644f1baf22534d9cb30142f440882d170d28bc6c\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-a-release-or-operating-contract\", \"title\": \"Prepare a release or operating contract\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-a-release-or-operating-contract\", \"start_line\": 166, \"end_line\": 220, \"content\": \"### Prepare a release or operating contract\\n\\n**Inputs:** A proposed release or ongoing operating obligation, its scope,\\nexisting work-order or requirement IDs, and any accepted contract that may\\nalready cover it.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** A completed release-contract (REL) or operating-contract\\n  (OPS) draft when needed. An accepted contract is reused only if its meaning\\n  and scope already cover the proposed obligation.\\n- **Transient working material:** Selection notes, new IDs and paths, and\\n  unresolved questions. No release or operating authorization is inferred.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Decide which obligation applies: release scope uses `release_contract`;\\n   continuing assurance uses `operating_contract`. Do not create both by default.\\n2. Read existing contracts selected for reuse. If an accepted contract needs\\n   changed meaning, use the accepted-definition amendment boundary; do not edit\\n   it through this draft-creation procedure.\\n3. For a missing contract, use the supported domain and artifact creation\\n   sequence from \\u201cDefine the change.\\u201d Inspect the dry-run result and use its\\n   returned `allocated_id` in the creation command.\\n4. Complete the generated body and accountable metadata. For a REL, record\\n   release scope, version conditions, rollback, and evidence expectations.\\n   For an OPS, record measurable observability, support, and operating obligations.\\n5. Set `REL.gates` to every existing work-order ID covered by the release\\n   contract, or `OPS.assures` to every existing requirement ID for which it\\n   claims continuing assurance. Do not leave invented or unresolved IDs.\\n6. Apply `## release_contract` or `## operating_contract` and its `### Checklist`\\n   in `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n7. Validate the completed draft and resolve findings within the proposed scope.\\n8. Include the contract in [Authorize the work](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#procedure) for the exact human decision.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nHere `TYPE` is `release_contract` or `operating_contract`, selected in action 1:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --id CONTRACT-ID --json\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\n```\\n\\n**Completion:** The applicable contract is covered by an unchanged accepted\\nrecord or a completed draft ready for its decision. Unresolved amendments\\nremain visible and block dependent work.\\n\\n**Later use:** An accepted REL governs release preparation. An accepted OPS\\ngoverns its stated continuing obligations after delivery. Perform the checks\\nand follow-up actions named in the OPS at its specified triggers; one successful\\ndelivery does not establish continuing conformance. External operating actions\\nstill require their exact authority.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"723a469b890666ae4b1e7b95a6231200a6794e6b792fef8e043ed82bc4f96ce5\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h44\\\\f\\\\codex-421\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"release_contract\", \"title\": \"release_contract\", \"anchor\": \"release_contract\", \"start_line\": 157, \"end_line\": 163, \"content\": \"## release_contract\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `gates` names every work order the release may include.\\n- Version, rollback conditions, and evidence expectations are explicit.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"c9c8d32b5f3c5b73f05f5d2cd120379bb50e81625a8d58d6c4d1ce25529a61f5\"}]}]}\r\n",

It does not\\nmean every change must create a new file. Reuse an existing active artifact\\nwhen its accepted meaning and scope still cover the work. Create a conditional\\nartifact only when its condition applies.\\n\\nFor an existing selected work order (WO), get its current state and next\\naction with:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nBefore implementation, check whether that work order (WO) and its linked\\ndefinitions are eligible to start:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl preflight REPO --work-order WO-ID --phase start --json\\n```\\n\\nThe first command reports lifecycle context without evaluating checkpoint\\ngates. The second evaluates start readiness, including the states and coverage\\nof the selected definitions. Neither command approves or starts work.\\nHere, `REPO` is the absolute repository path and `WO-ID` is the actual ID of\\nthe selected work order (WO). Use the repository's selected released evaluator.\\n\\n| Type                  | ID prefix | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                      | When needed                                                                                                                                              |\\n|-----------------------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `intent`              | `INT-`    | States the problem, intended outcome, and limits of responsibility.                                                                                                          | The work needs an accepted purpose. Reuse an intent (INT) when that purpose still applies.                                                               |\\n| `capability`          | `CAP-`    | Describes an ability that a human or agent should have.                                                                                                                      | Requirements (REQ) need a link to the capability (CAP) they support.                                                                                     |\\n| `requirement`         | `REQ-`    | States required behavior or a constraint, with a condition for acceptance.                                                                                                   | The change creates or changes an obligation. Reuse a requirement (REQ) only if its meaning stays unchanged.                                              |\\n| `specification`       | `SPEC-`   | Defines the detailed behavior, interfaces, constraints, and rejection conditions.                                                                                            | Each requirement (REQ) selected for implementation needs specification (SPEC) coverage.                                                                  |\\n| `architecture`        | `ARCH-`   | Defines system structure and boundaries needed to meet significant requirements (REQ).                                                                                       | An active architecture (ARCH) directly addresses a requirement (REQ) selected by the work order (WO).                                                    |\\n| `adr`                 | `ADR-`    | Records an architecture decision (ADR), the alternatives, and their consequences.                                                                                            | An applicable architecture (ARCH) declares that a significant decision is required.                                                                      |\\n| `verification`        | `VER-`    | Defines how requirements (REQ) will be checked and what counts as a pass.                                                                                                    | Each selected requirement (REQ) needs verification coverage. This is the verification contract (VER), not a test result.                                 |\\n| `work_order`          | `WO-`     | Defines the bounded work to execute and its governing artifacts. Approval grants work authority.                                                                             | Before execution. One work order (WO) may cover several requirements (REQ). Completed scope does not authorize later work.                               |\\n| `verification_record` | `VREC-`   | Binds work orders (WO), verification contracts (VER), evidence, and one exact candidate commit for assessment.                                                               | When verification tied to a commit is required. One record may cover several work orders (WO) at the same commit.                                        |\\n| `release_contract`    | `REL-`    | Defines permitted release scope, gates, rollback conditions, and authority limits.                                                                                           | When a release record (RLS) is proposed.                                                                                                                 |\\n| `release_record`      | `RLS-`    | Records preparation and the later release decision for verified work at one exact commit.                                                                                    | When a formal release is proposed. Preparing the record does not release the work.                                                                       |\\n| `decision`            | `DEC-`    | Records a question, options, recommendation, decision maker, affected artifacts, and the eventual answer. It can also record a deviation from one specification (SPEC) rule. | A question blocks a transition, affects more than one artifact, or must remain recorded after approval; or work cannot meet a specification (SPEC) rule. |\\n| `risk`                | `RISK-`   | Records a threat, an owner, and a next action. Scoring and categories are optional.                                                                                          | A concern needs follow-up. A separate decision (DEC) is used when the concern must block work.                                                           |\\n| `operating_contract`  | `OPS-`    | Defines continuing service, support, monitoring, or operational assurance obligations.                                                                                       | Ongoing operational commitments apply. Omitting the record does not prove those commitments have been met.                                               |\\n\\nCode, tests, acceptance scenarios, evidence files, commits, dashboards, tickets,\\nand conversations are not additional formal artifact types. They may support\\nor be referenced by formal artifacts but do not grant authority by themselves.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"47268c9ec1e3551fb547ad3d1ef7b8da0b773b52b3a4364f42c36cc64f98bf83\"}, {\"heading\": \"artifact-locations\", \"title\": \"Artifact locations\", \"anchor\": \"artifact-locations\", \"start_line\": 63, \"end_line\": 96, \"content\": \"## Artifact locations\\n\\nNew formal artifacts use these directories below\\n`docs/engineering/DOMAIN/`. `DOMAIN` is the selected domain name. These paths\\ndescribe storage, not authority; the artifact ID, metadata, and typed links\\nremain authoritative. Use the supported authoring command to obtain the actual\\npath. Do not move existing records merely to match this table.\\n\\n| Artifact | TYPE | Directory |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Intent (INT) | `intent` | `intent/` |\\n| Capability (CAP) | `capability` | `capabilities/` |\\n| Requirement (REQ) | `requirement` | `requirements/` |\\n| Specification (SPEC) | `specification` | `specifications/` |\\n| Architecture (ARCH) | `architecture` | `architecture/` |\\n| Architecture decision (ADR) | `adr` | `architecture/adr/` |\\n| Verification contract (VER) | `verification` | `verification/` |\\n| Work order (WO) | `work_order` | `work-orders/` |\\n| Verification record (VREC) | `verification_record` | `verification-records/` |\\n| Release contract (REL) | `release_contract` | `release/` |\\n| Release record (RLS) | `release_record` | `releases/` |\\n| Operating contract (OPS) | `operating_contract` | `operations/` |\\n| Decision (DEC) | `decision` | `decisions/` |\\n| Risk (RISK) | `risk` | `risks/` |\\n\\nThe same domain has `evidence/` for retained work-order evidence and\\n`acceptance/` for acceptance scenarios. These are supporting files, not new\\nformal artifact types. Legacy flat artifact locations remain readable and\\nMUST NOT be moved by an upgrade without separate authority.\\n\\nTemplates under `docs/engineering/templates/` are authoring assets. They are\\nexcluded from active-artifact validation and grant no authority. Use\\n`capture-verification` and `prepare-release` for commit-bound VREC and RLS\\ninstances; an edited template is not a substitute for their derived evidence.\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8df276d2f837c4dcc663dbdb42c67cbb6f8fe3bf4abcb53acf86bc7538269a72\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/DEFINITION_LINKS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h44\\\\f\\\\codex-421\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\DEFINITION_LINKS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"75b0c06f90fbb219fc31684a1a2d97987215dbada20e335656e45a57532c3010\", \"bytes\": 3505, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"links-between-definitions\", \"title\": \"Links between definitions\", \"anchor\": \"links-between-definitions\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 35, \"content\": \"## Links between definitions\\n\\nAn arrow points from the artifact that records the link to the artifact it\\nreferences. These links describe meaning and coverage, not execution order.\\n\\nRepository validation, draft validation and work-order preflight share the\\ndeclared source/relation/target types. A supplied undeclared relation or a target\\nof the wrong type is invalid even when no work order selects the artifact.\\nPreflight still evaluates readiness only for its selected governing chain.\\nThe read-only draft query permits specific unfinished authoring slots; ordinary\\nvalidation and approval retain their completeness requirements.\\n\\n```mermaid\\nflowchart LR\\n    CAP[\\\"Capability (CAP)\\\"] -->|derives_from| INT[\\\"Intent (INT)\\\"]\\n    REQ[\\\"Requirement (REQ)\\\"] -->|derives_from| CAP\\n    SPEC[\\\"Specification (SPEC)\\\"] -->|specifies| REQ\\n    VER[\\\"Verification contract (VER)\\\"] -->|verifies| REQ\\n    ARCH[\\\"Architecture (ARCH)\\\"] -->|addresses| REQ\\n    ARCH -->|conforms_to| SPEC\\n    ADR[\\\"Architecture decision (ADR)\\\"] -->|decides| ARCH\\n```\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Capability (CAP) \\u2192 Intent (INT) | `derives_from` | Each active capability (CAP) names one or more active intents (INT). |\\n| Requirement (REQ) \\u2192 Capability (CAP) | `derives_from` | Each active requirement (REQ) names one or more active capabilities (CAP). |\\n| Specification (SPEC) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `specifies` | Each requirement (REQ) selected by a work order (WO) needs one or more selected active specifications (SPEC). |\\n| Architecture (ARCH) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `addresses` | The architecture (ARCH) names every requirement (REQ) that materially drives its structure. |\\n| Architecture (ARCH) \\u2192 Specification (SPEC) | `conforms_to` | For each addressed requirement (REQ), the selected architecture (ARCH) names at least one selected specification (SPEC) covering it. |\\n| Architecture decision (ADR) \\u2192 Architecture (ARCH) | `decides` | Each selected architecture (ARCH) that requires a design decision has at least one selected active architecture decision (ADR). |\\n| Verification contract (VER) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `verifies` | Each selected requirement (REQ) has one or more selected active verification contracts (VER). |\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"7e7361437700c3a1bf7d9add02accf3a4d3ee3fa48dbdc0ba0b991b40514071a\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h44\\\\f\\\\codex-421\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"design-simplicity\", \"title\": \"Design simplicity\", \"anchor\": \"design-simplicity\", \"start_line\": 21, \"end_line\": 58, \"content\": \"## Design simplicity\\n\\nFor unfinished work, `harnessctl validate-draft REPO --artifact ID --json`\\nreports whether one supported draft has an admissible shape. Only exact values\\nat the same type and field in this evaluator's canonical template, and missing\\nor empty required authoring links, can be reported as incomplete. Invalid\\nidentity, dates, metadata shapes, actual endpoints, lifecycle history and\\ndisposition are errors. A missing non-template ID is an error. Background\\nfindings remain visible; this result makes no whole-repository validity claim.\\nComplete the authoring checklist and pass ordinary approval gates before\\nrequesting approval. Draft admission grants no authority to write or approve.\\n\\nChoose the least complex design that satisfies the agreed requirements and\\nconstraints. Justify material added complexity by the need it serves and why\\na simpler approach is insufficient. Consider the effort to understand, build,\\ntest, operate and change the whole solution. Defer speculative needs. Review\\nboth the necessity of the specified behavior and the simplicity of its\\nimplementation. Preserve correctness and the project's required quality and\\nsafety properties.\\n\\nStart from the smallest complete solution. Each project supplies its agreed\\nusers, scale, operating conditions and quality constraints. Agreed future needs\\ncan matter; imagined flexibility alone is insufficient. Credible risk analysis\\ncan justify prevention before an incident. Fewer lines, shorter specifications\\nor fewer tests do not establish simplicity; moving work to users, operations\\nor dependencies also has a cost.\\n\\nApply the relevant questions below before definition approval and during design\\nand implementation review. Return unjustified obligations or design complexity\\nfor revision through the existing decision process. Explain material choices\\nin the existing specification, design or review: the need, why a simpler option\\nis insufficient and the added cost. Scale the explanation to the decision; a\\nsmall choice may need one sentence, a significant design may use its existing\\narchitecture decision. Trivial changes need no separate comparison document.\\n\\nThese are human review standards. They introduce no separate KISS artifact,\\nmandatory score, receipt, automated simplicity gate or additional approval.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"29e9b6296f39215c4b2ad36659c0674f0b20650682db9aa1187fc97871cfdb06\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/DELIVER_RESULT.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h44\\\\f\\\\codex-421\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\DELIVER_RESULT.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"13405ba32a2227a5c20abb59e806de18ed60b4ecf3c010508f053587cd8bf6b2\", \"bytes\": 12123, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nA delivery path is selected or its exact external action needs preparation, authority or readback.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ead6dc699ad51b30b9deca478ada5107ea915cf305c8d2365602961d48f68d2e\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nBefore any external action, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and the repository instructions for that action. Read the exact selected candidate, verification or release record.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"088b0023cee60e9d78ebb2916dd2db983e71274c32128f7d0e8f6d4144535b62\"}, {\"heading\": \"select-the-delivery-action\", \"title\": \"Select the delivery action\", \"anchor\": \"select-the-delivery-action\", \"start_line\": 43, \"end_line\": 79, \"content\": \"### Select the delivery action\\n\\n**Inputs:** The requested delivery, selected work or verification record,\\ncandidate identity, and intended destination.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** None changed.\\n- **Transient working material:** One named action, its exact candidate or\\n  release identity, destination, selected procedure, and required authority.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Inspect the selected work order (WO), verification record (VREC), or release\\n   record (RLS) with the command below.\\n2. Name the action: for example, create a pull request, merge, prepare a\\n   release, tag, publish, or deploy.\\n3. Identify the full candidate commit or immutable release identity.\\n4. Identify the exact target repository and ref, registry, or deployment environment.\\n5. Read the repository's instructions for that delivery action.\\n6. Select the matching procedure or a complete alternative declared by the\\n   evaluator. Resolve an ambiguous destination with the requester.\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact ARTIFACT-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse a work order (WO), verification record (VREC), or release record (RLS)\\nas `ARTIFACT-ID`. Selection changes no lifecycle state.\\n\\n**Completion:** One delivery action and target are explicit. Selecting a path\\ndoes not authorize or perform its external action.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Prepare the delivery package](DELIVER_RESULT.md#prepare-the-delivery-package), [Obtain the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#obtain-the-release-decision-when-required), [Record the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#record-the-release-decision-when-required), [Confirm authority for the external action](DELIVER_RESULT.md#confirm-authority-for-the-external-action), [Perform the authorized delivery](DELIVER_RESULT.md#perform-the-authorized-delivery), [Confirm the delivery result](DELIVER_RESULT.md#confirm-the-delivery-result) prepare, authorize, perform, and confirm that action.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"3c62d9982634dc649143dfbaa6d84299d868a5b1f9f4d18861c99d673da2f01d\"}]}]}\r\n",
  "exit_code": 0,
  "status": "completed"
}

  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/AUTHORIZE_WORK.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h44\\\\f\\\\codex-421\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\AUTHORIZE_WORK.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"991b526d6280554dcca6901c1790e5519b8894e08635a1f10618aa84a29aaf28\", \"bytes\": 15212, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nThe proposed package needs validation, review or a human authorization decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8b18d925f39f314acc9ea6bcc9820015c4c9430d836144e85bc31b670752371b\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nFor reviewing each definition, use its selected [Type checklist](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#type-checklists). Before review, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and [AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation](AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation). Before approving work, read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification). For an open or deferred decision, read [RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"9aa32693606102a5aa74b2e4a614aed6904471e5f618dea93356baac97c86ca2\"}, {\"heading\": \"assess-the-proposed-artifact-package\", \"title\": \"Assess the proposed artifact package\", \"anchor\": \"assess-the-proposed-artifact-package\", \"start_line\": 32, \"end_line\": 83, \"content\": \"### Assess the proposed artifact package\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected work order (WO) IDs, proposed definitions, validation\\nresults, and existing decision records (DEC).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** None created or modified.\\n- **Transient working material:** A review list identifying the selected\\n  artifacts, their states, applicable checks, and reported blockers.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Run validation for the repository.\\n2. Inspect each selected work order (WO) with the command below.\\n3. Read the work order (WO) and its returned reading manifest.\\n4. Review the governing definitions against the relevant checklists in\\n   `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n5. Check that the proposed work has defined scope, verification coverage,\\n   assurance classification, and accountable humans for the required decisions.\\n6. List the blockers affecting the selected package. Keep unrelated findings\\n   separate.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --checkpoint transition --target approved --json\\n```\\n\\nRead the result of each required check. A `pass` satisfies that check only;\\nit does not approve the artifacts or authorize implementation. If a required\\ncheck returns `fail` or `not_assessable`, report its identifier and stated\\nreason, then follow \\u201cIf a procedure is blocked.\\u201d Do not proceed with the\\naffected approval.\\n\\nThe last command evaluates work-order approval gates. A checkpoint-free\\n`check` only reports lifecycle context. Definition artifacts cannot be selected\\nwith `check`; their transition gates are evaluated by the previews in [Apply the selected transitions](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#apply-the-selected-transitions).\\n\\nBefore proposing a definition for approval, resolve its template placeholders.\\nIf it contains an `Open decisions` section, confirm that no unresolved decision\\nremains before setting that section to `None`. Do not remove an unresolved\\nquestion merely to make validation pass.\\n\\n**Completion:** The selected package has an explicit list of review findings\\nand approval blockers. No approval is inferred from these checks.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Resolve approval blockers](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#resolve-approval-blockers) resolves the blockers. [Obtain the human's decision](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#obtain-the-humans-decision) presents the package for a\\nhuman decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"2ea6b051236e13dd427317722d16ce7941ef5a4eb4789f7fdf568ab3d0cae3c0\"}, {\"heading\": \"apply-the-selected-transitions\", \"title\": \"Apply the selected transitions\", \"anchor\": \"apply-the-selected-transitions\", \"start_line\": 221, \"end_line\": 270, \"content\": \"### Apply the selected transitions\\n\\n**Inputs:** The exact artifact IDs, target states, accountable human identities,\\nreviewed file digests, decisions from [Obtain the human's decision](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#obtain-the-humans-decision), and clarification answers from\\n[Define the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#procedure) that must be retained in the transition reason.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only explicitly selected definitions and work orders\\n  (WO) receive the applied state and lifecycle-history entries.\\n- **Transient working material:** The preview and apply results, including\\n  any refused transition.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Confirm that the reviewed artifact contents still match the human decision.\\n2. Select only the named transitions. Approve governing definitions before\\n   dependent work, or use one explicitly selected packet for mutually\\n   dependent definitions when the evaluator permits it.\\n3. Preview the transition command below.\\n4. Compare every selected ID, target state, actor, and reported effect with\\n   the human decision. Resolve failed gates before proceeding.\\n5. Recheck reviewed definition digests immediately before applying.\\n6. Repeat the passing command with `--apply`. Do not add related artifacts\\n   that the human did not select.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set ARTIFACT-ID=TARGET --decision ARTIFACT-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set ARTIFACT-ID=TARGET --decision ARTIFACT-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\n```\\n\\nFor each clarification below the formal-decision threshold, add\\n`--reason \\\"ARTIFACT-ID=Question and confirmed answer\\\"` to both the preview\\nand apply command. Use the actual question and answer. When one artifact\\nhas several such answers, combine them into one reason value for that ID.\\nKeep each complete `ID=TEXT` value as one argument. Confirm the saved reason\\nin the resulting lifecycle entry before discarding the working notes.\\n\\nFor approval, `TARGET` is `approved`. For rejection, use `rejected` and add\\n`--reason \\\"ARTIFACT-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to both commands. Rejection is\\nterminal. For a packet, repeat `--set` and `--decision` for every explicitly\\nselected artifact. Preview and apply must contain the same assignments.\\n\\n**Completion:** The evaluator reports the actual applied transitions, or the\\nspecific refusal. A successful preview alone changes nothing.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Confirm the authorization result](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#confirm-the-authorization-result) confirms the resulting authority and readiness.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"c5215dec9f35d1a99bf6e4d658a594a31dc544131e70db49b1b8f79514e124b8\"}]}]}\r\n",

  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/RELEASE.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h44\\\\f\\\\codex-421\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\RELEASE.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"ce700f8f764c4425978f070d978d48eacafb927601f45e298c765f46dae90f7f\", \"bytes\": 7849, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nThe evaluator selects release-record preparation or a decision on a ready release record.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"6aca380f7ecb033e57e7e4bf6aca16914111bae9e93070270f93b5380517c210\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nBefore preparing, read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#release-coverage](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#release-coverage) and the selected REL/VREC records. Before a release decision, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and [AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation](AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ddbc0b4cafdf1d5c05a185936aa8cb848c0028eeca29b9bc05ee6365782404b0\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-a-release-record\", \"title\": \"Prepare a release record\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-a-release-record\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 71, \"content\": \"### Prepare a release record\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected path, existing preparation authority, exact candidate,\\nand the release contract (REL) and eligible verified coverage required by that\\npath. Release-record preparation requires both.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Release path:** One release record (RLS) in `ready` and its generated\\n  evaluator evidence, when preparation is required and succeeds.\\n- **Retained files:** Required build or delivery evidence at the authorized\\n  locations. Builds occur only when separately covered by the selected scope.\\n- **Transient working material:** Preparation notes, proposed external content,\\n  and inspected write destinations.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Confirm authority for the exact preparation operation. Obtain a missing\\n   human decision before writing; reuse matching authority already supplied.\\n2. Inspect existing records and outputs before creating replacements.\\n3. For release, select an active release contract (REL), version, domain,\\n   and unused release record (RLS) ID. Check local Git refs and existing\\n   version reservations before choosing the ID and version.\\n4. Select the final eligible verification record (VREC) for the candidate.\\n   Its work-order (WO) set must exactly cover the work being released.\\n5. Confirm all intended output paths and the clean working-tree condition\\n   required by release preparation.\\n6. Run the release preparation command. Inspect its written record, evidence,\\n   candidate identity, and `ready` state.\\n7. Retain the new release record (RLS) and evidence in an authorized governance\\n   commit after the candidate they describe.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor release preparation:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl prepare-release REPO --id RLS-ID --release-contract REL-ID --verification-record VREC-ID --work-order WO-ID --version VERSION --owner ACTOR --domain DOMAIN --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse the actual preparation actor for `--owner`. Preparation does not record\\na future verification or release decision. Preserve the generated record and\\nits bound evidence without changing the recorded evidence bytes.\\n\\nRepeat `--work-order` for every released work order (WO). This evaluator requires one final verification record (VREC) covering the complete\\nrelease. Earlier records remain supporting evidence. If that coverage is\\nmissing, return to verification instead of inventing or relabelling it.\\n\\nAdd `--tag TAG` only for an explicitly selected tag value; this records the\\nvalue and does not create a Git tag. `prepare-release` writes after its checks;\\nit has no `--dry-run` or `--apply` option.\\n\\n**Completion:** The required delivery inputs are prepared, or a precise\\npreparation blocker is known. Preparation performs no merge, publication,\\ndeployment, or release decision.\\n\\n**Later use:** A ready release record (RLS) proceeds to [Obtain the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#obtain-the-release-decision-when-required). \\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d3fcc6f4d9565acc0d714479b8b27df0173ce927ec4d36a757bf1f5710f34942\"}]}]}\r\n",
  "exit_code": 0,

}

  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/RELEASE.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\h44\\\\f\\\\codex-421\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\RELEASE.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"ce700f8f764c4425978f070d978d48eacafb927601f45e298c765f46dae90f7f\", \"bytes\": 7849, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"read-this-when\", \"title\": \"Read this when\", \"anchor\": \"read-this-when\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 6, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Read this when\\n\\nThe evaluator selects release-record preparation or a decision on a ready release record.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"6aca380f7ecb033e57e7e4bf6aca16914111bae9e93070270f93b5380517c210\"}, {\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"entry_condition\": true, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nBefore preparing, read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#release-coverage](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#release-coverage) and the selected REL/VREC records. Before a release decision, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and [AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation](AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ddbc0b4cafdf1d5c05a185936aa8cb848c0028eeca29b9bc05ee6365782404b0\"}, {\"heading\": \"obtain-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"title\": \"Obtain the release decision, when required\", \"anchor\": \"obtain-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"start_line\": 72, \"end_line\": 116, \"content\": \"### Obtain the release decision, when required\\n\\n**Inputs:** The ready release record (RLS), release contract (REL), candidate,\\nverified coverage, version, and accountable human's release authority.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** None changed by review or the gate check.\\n- **Transient working material:** The human's exact release or rejection\\n  decision, including the reason for rejection.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Present the candidate, included work, verification coverage, version,\\n   constraints, rollback conditions, and required release evidence.\\n   If the contract and delivery plan select complete release delivery, follow\\n   [Complete-release authority](AUTHORITY.md#complete-release-authority). Finish\\n   required deliverable preparation and human verification before this request.\\n   Show one concise request: \\\"Approve the complete release\\\", its versions,\\n   delivery actions, verification summary, limitations and a link to the exact\\n   plan. Include payload digests, destinations, marker targets and any bounded\\n   release-only integration in that plan.\\n2. Run the transition gate check for the intended target state.\\n3. Obtain the accountable human's decision on the selected release record\\n   (RLS). Reuse a matching decision already supplied.\\n   For complete delivery, the same response explicitly covers its listed external\\n   actions. Retain the actual human, decision reference and reviewed plan digest.\\n   Do not rewrite the plan when public observations arrive; retain them separately.\\n4. Retain a rejection reason when applicable.\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --checkpoint transition --target TARGET --json\\n```\\n\\nUse `released` or `rejected` for `TARGET`, according to the proposed decision.\\nThe evaluator determines legality. A passed check does not supply approval.\\n\\n**Completion:** The release decision is explicit, or remains pending.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Record the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#record-the-release-decision-when-required) records that decision. Execute listed delivery actions\\nunder the same complete-release authorization when their conditions still match.\\nOtherwise obtain only the exact external authority that is missing.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"3f8f1bc33363c8583a4b28560220ccaa7497990299624c53d90e1b364fecca78\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"title\": \"Record the release decision, when required\", \"anchor\": \"record-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"start_line\": 117, \"end_line\": 159, \"content\": \"### Record the release decision, when required\\n\\n**Inputs:** The human's exact decision and unchanged release inputs.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only the selected release record (RLS) receives the\\n  permitted state and lifecycle-history entry.\\n- **Retained files:** The updated release record (RLS), retained through\\n  authorized Git actions.\\n- **Transient working material:** The applied result and current next action.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Compare the current release inputs with the human's reviewed inputs.\\n2. Preview the selected transition.\\n3. Apply the same command when its gates pass and effects match the decision.\\n4. Inspect the release record (RLS) and report the actual resulting state.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set RLS-ID=TARGET --decision RLS-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set RLS-ID=TARGET --decision RLS-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nFor rejection, add `--reason \\\"RLS-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to both transition\\ncommands. Related verification records (VREC) and work orders (WO) are not\\ntransitioned automatically.\\n\\nFor a complete-release decision, use the existing `--reason` input to retain the\\nactual human decision reference and reviewed delivery-plan path and SHA-256.\\nThis is retained evidence of the supplied decision, not permission derived by\\nparsing arbitrary reason text. Preserve the referenced plan bytes for each later\\nauthority comparison. No new approval file or lifecycle state is needed.\\n\\n**Completion:** The release decision is recorded or explicitly refused.\\nNo Git tag, publication, or deployment has been performed by this transition.\\n\\n**Later use:** A released record may support [Confirm authority for the external action](DELIVER_RESULT.md#confirm-authority-for-the-external-action)'s external-action checks.\\nRejection follows the evaluator's remediation procedure.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"41884593e91b2762c5d0406d1b6e73f0f7731edf06676a4cf15a64b0760c789d\"}]}]}\r\n",

A partial response cannot support that claim.\\nIf the host saves or truncates a response, inspect the returned file through an\\navailable, permitted read tool. A saved-file notice or successful tool call does\\nnot establish completeness. For large JSON, extract the result metadata without\\nloading the whole graph into the conversation. If the response cannot be read,\\nreport its completeness as unassessed; do not report unseen content or use it to\\nsupport a governing claim.\\n\\nRetain the view,\\nrevision and evaluator identities and report the embedded released result unchanged.\\nAn accepted read is not an approval. Database-side read-only enforcement remains\\nunverified under RISK-HAG-001; use only the private public-data sandbox.\\n\\nBefore writing the results report, read and apply\\n[Report observed results](../../evidence/references/hosted-evidence.md#report-observed-results).\\n\\n### Read one hosted revision\\n\\nUse the exact `view`, artifact ID and revision ID returned by the selected\\noperation. Typed CLI read takes `--artifact ID --expected-revision REVISION`\\nand either `--baseline ID` or `--context ID --context-version N`. Add `--typed\\n--compact --record-directory NEW_DIRECTORY` to retain the exact response and\\ndecoded document. Read the returned text, or its local path when large.\\nInspect completeness, continuation, view and revision identity before authoring.\\nThe client checks decoded bytes against the envelope's document digest.\\n\\nRaw `remote read --request FILE` and the read-only revision MCP tool remain\\navailable. Their v1 schema is the `revision` branch of `$defs.Request` in\\n`server/contracts/read-v1.json`, with RequestFields, View and Budget.
